'''Merc Coin''' is an earnable currency introduced with [[Operations]]. Commanders receive Merc Coins for successfully completing Operations and spend them on MercGear modules and specialised Engineering Blueprints.<ref name="frontier-operations">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/update-notes/4-4-0-0 Frontier Developments: Elite Dangerous: Operations — Available Now], accessed 13 September 2026.</ref>

Merc Coin is not a Raw, Manufactured, Encoded, or Odyssey Engineering material. It is also not an ARX currency and cannot be purchased for ARX.<ref name="frontier-preview">[https://www.elitedangerous.com/news/update-operations Frontier Developments: An Update on Operations], accessed 13 September 2026.</ref>

== Earning Merc Coins ==

Merc Coins are awarded when an Operation is completed successfully. Operations can be launched alone or with a squad, with optional matchmaking available to fill open positions.

The amount and distribution of rewards depend on the selected Operation and its difficulty. Hard Operations provide greater reward value than their Easy versions, but the scenario itself is also a major factor.<ref name="frontier-operations" />

Merc Coins are awarded alongside other possible Operation rewards:

* credits;
* Engineering materials;
* Powerplay Merits when an eligible Operation is completed in Powerplay Mode.

The live reward screen is authoritative for the payout attached to a particular Operation.

== Spending Merc Coins ==

Merc Coins are spent through existing vendors rather than a separate Merc store:

* '''Outfitting''' sells eligible MercGear ship modules.
* '''Engineers''' sell eligible Merc Engineering Blueprints.

Purchased equipment begins at its base level. Compatible MercGear can then be upgraded by the appropriate Engineer as more Merc Coins are earned. A Merc-only Blueprint applies only to compatible Merc modules; it does not turn an ordinary version of the module into the Merc variant.

== MercGear catalogue ==

The Operations launch catalogue included two Merc Blueprints:

* Thermal Plasma Conversion for Beam, Burst, and Pulse Lasers;
* Scoop Rate Enhanced for Fuel Scoops.

The initial pre-engineered equipment catalogue included specialised hardpoints, core modules, and optional internals. Examples include:

* the Far-Reaching [[Abrasion Blaster]] and Long Range [[Mining Laser]];
* an Enduring Feedback Rail Gun and several specialised missile racks;
* Focused and Balanced [[Power Distributor|Power Distributors]];
* an Extended Cargo Rack, Long Range [[Detailed Surface Scanner]], and Heavy Duty Module Reinforcement Package.

Frontier has stated that the catalogue can expand as Operations develops. Check the relevant Outfitting or Engineer interface for current availability and prices rather than relying on a static shopping list.<ref name="frontier-operations" />

== Planning purchases ==

Before spending Merc Coins:

# Confirm that the reward is a module or a Blueprint.
# Check which Engineer handles the module family and Merc Blueprint.
# Account for the module's base characteristics and any fixed pre-engineered trade-offs.
# Compare the MercGear item with an ordinary engineered module in the intended ship build.
# Retain enough Merc Coins for the complete set of purchases or upgrades the build requires.

A MercGear item is not automatically better for every ship. Its value depends on slot size, power, mass, heat, ammunition, and the fixed modifiers attached to that specific variant.
